name: Giog
summary: Four-player trick-taking game played with 32 Xiangqi pieces used as cards, won by capturing pieces with higher combinations.
rules_text: Use 32 Xiangqi discs shuffled face-down. Build paired stacks in rows per player and determine seating order by revealing bottom pieces from other rows, highest rank first. First player takes an end stack and stacks are taken clockwise until each has 8 pieces (10 with three players, 12 with two). Ranks high to low: general 帥>將>guards 仕>士>ministers 相>象>chariots 俥>車>horses 傌>馬>cannons 炮>砲>soldiers 兵>卒, red beats black of same type. Valid leads: single, pair of identical pieces, triple identical soldiers/pawns, four and five identical, or Giog triple of one colour: general+guard+elephant, cannon+guard+elephant, chariot+horse+cannon. Leader plays 1-5 face-down and announces type if three pieces. Others in any order play same count face-down, cannot include general on first/last trick. Reveal; highest combination of same type as lead wins, leader wins ties, else seat order breaks ties. General cannot be played first or last trick or scorer scores zero. Play until hands empty.
rating_reason: Specific trick-taking game using pieces as cards, turn-based strategy
